- Commercial: predictable unit economics or Dedicated capacity option if throughput warrants

Immediate asks from our side
- Please share the org chart / stakeholder list (economic buyer, procurement contact, security reviewer).
- Any firm blackout dates for procurement/legal review windows in Q1?

What we'll send by EOD
- Stakeholder mapping template (attached: redwood_stakeholder_template.xlsx)

Thanks — I'll follow up with the MAP and SOC2 summary.

- Economic buyer: Samir Patel (CIO) — he'll own the final approval and budget.

Emily — perfect, thanks for the org chart and clarity on owners. Next steps from our side:

1) Security + Procurement alignment call
- Purpose: walk through SOC2 summary, network controls, DPA specifics, and procurement requirements
- Attendees suggested: Claire (security), procurement rep, Samir (optional), Rishi (security lead at Redwood), and myself
- Proposed times: Thu 9-11am PT or Fri 1-3pm PT — tell me what works and I'll send a calendar invite.

2) Docs I'm sharing now
- redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf (high-level controls and audit scope)
- redwood_MAP_v1.pdf (draft MAP with milestones: security review, pilot, procurement/PO)

3) Commercial note (high level)
- We can support both Hosted API (usage-based) and Dedicated Reserved capacity (for predictable throughput). Rishi will share a quick pricing range so procurement has an anchor.

If you can confirm the procurement contact person (name + phone) and whether there are standard contract terms we should expect (e.g., insurance limits, indemnity), that will speed the procurement review.

I'll also prepare a short one-pager on encryption at-rest / KMS options for Claire.

Thanks — I'll send the calendar invite once you confirm availability.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf, redwood_MAP_v1.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhou <e.zhou@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Stakeholder mapping request + follow-up from demo

Hi Emily — quick note from the security/commercial side to give procurement an initial anchor:

- Hosted API (usage) — typical entry: $0.0025–$0.012 per token-equivalent depending on model family and throughput; suitable for evaluation/pilot.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) — for predictable high-throughput use cases we typically structure a committed monthly spend with discounts; example starting point $25K–$75K/mo depending on GPU footprint and SLA.

These are high-level ranges — we can refine after we understand expected monthly request volume, average sequence lengths, and latency SLOs. If procurement can share an expected QPS or monthly token estimate, we can model a recommended configuration and pricing.

I'll join the security/procurement call and bring our SOC2 artifact set and encryption/KMS details. Suggested next step: confirm one of Marissa's proposed time windows and send invite.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
